transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I hope I'm not wasting your time, but I guess what finally made me ask for help is... well, I just keep forgetting little things. Just silly things I normally handle fine. 

I mean, it's not a huge disaster or anything, I'm still getting my work done! But... like, I'll forget to return calls, or I'll completely forget to turn in a registration form. Or even just personal stuff, like stopping for an errand on the way home. 

I'm a secretary, so I really try to be on top of everything, and I feel terrible when I drop the ball. I don't want people to think I'm slacking. It's just been happening a bit more lately, and I thought I should probably ask someone about it. Is that... does that make sense to come in for?
How long have you been noticing these problems with forgetting little things?

Um, well... I guess I'd say it's been about fifteen months? Give or take? I started taking an evening certificate program back then to, you know, try and improve my skills for work. And I guess... well, ever since I added that to my plate, keeping on top of all the little organization things has just been noticeably harder to manage. 

I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining or that I can't handle hard work, because I promise I usually can! It's just... juggling the classes and my regular job, it feels like my brain gets a little too full, if that makes sense? I hope it's okay that I'm bringing it up... is it normal to get a little scattered when you take on extra classes like that?
Are you noticing any problems with forgetting things in your personal life, outside of work and school?

Um... not really? I mean, I guess I'm pretty okay at home. I make sure to keep up with the laundry and grocery shopping and all that. Sometimes I might forget to, like, water a plant or call my sister back right away, but nothing major, I promise! 

I really try to keep my personal life neat so it doesn't spill over and cause problems. I hope that's the right answer? I just haven't noticed it being a big issue outside of the work and school stuff.
How are you feeling about these instances where you forget things, are you feeling anxious or stressed about them?

Um, well... I guess I am a little stressed about it, yeah. I mean, I'm still getting by! I really want to make that clear, I'm not, like, failing my classes or getting fired or anything awful like that. I'm handling it! 

But... I guess I do worry a bit because I've missed enough small work follow-ups and little school deadlines that... well, I just don't want it to affect my reputation, you know? I really pride myself on being reliable. And I've been hoping to maybe move up into an Office Manager role eventually, so I just... I want to make sure I'm putting my best foot forward. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm making a big deal out of nothing. Is it okay to be a little worried about that?
Do you find yourself having trouble focusing or paying attention during tasks?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I really do try my best to stay completely focused, I promise! But... sometimes, especially at the office or when I'm sitting in class, it doesn't take much to kind of... pull me away from what I'm working on. 

Like, if just one phone rings down the hall, or if I hear people talking nearby, I'll completely lose my place. Or even just... I don't know, a random thought about something at home will pop into my head, and suddenly I realize I'm not looking at my work anymore. 

I always catch myself and get right back to it, though! I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around daydreaming or slacking off. It's just a little hard to tune the little things out sometimes. I figure everyone gets a little sidetracked in a busy office, right? I hope that answers your question okay?
Do you have trouble remembering things that happened recently?

Um... no, not really. I mean, my memory for things that just happened is actually pretty good, I think! Like, if you ask me what I had for breakfast or what my boss told me this morning, I can tell you right away. 

I'm really careful about making sure I remember conversations and things that happen day-to-day. I know I mentioned getting distracted and missing a few little deadlines, but my actual memory is totally fine, I promise! I don't want to make it sound like I'm walking around completely forgetful or anything. I hope it's okay that I don't have a problem with that part?
Do you ever feel mentally foggy or like your thinking is cloudy?

Um, no, I wouldn't say that. I don't really feel foggy or... cloudy, or anything like that. My head usually feels pretty clear! 

I mean, I might get a little scattered when it's super busy at the office, but my thoughts themselves are sharp. I'm definitely not walking around in a daze or anything. I can always figure out what I need to do, it's just sometimes I get a little sidetracked along the way, like I mentioned. But my thinking is totally fine! Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have you been feeling overwhelmed or emotionally drained lately?

Um, overwhelmed? Oh, no, I don't think so. I mean, I guess everyone gets a little tired after a long week, right? But I wouldn't say I'm emotionally drained at all. 

I really try to keep a positive attitude, you know? Even when things get a bit hectic at work with all the filing and answering the phones, I just try to take a deep breath and keep smiling. I definitely don't want to complain or sound like I can't handle my job, because I really do like it! I just... I try to stay upbeat. I hope that makes sense? I'm doing okay, really!
Have you been having trouble learning new things for your certificate program or at work?

Um... no, not at all! Learning new things is actually something I really enjoy. I mean, I don't have a certificate program right now, but at work, if they show me a new phone system or a different way to do the filing, I catch on pretty quick!

I always try my best to pay close attention when someone is training me. I definitely don't want them to think I'm slow or can't keep up, you know? I might have to write a little note down just to make sure I do it exactly right, but I don't have any real trouble learning it. I think I do a pretty good job of picking up new tasks when they need me to! Does that sound okay? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.
Do you ever find yourself struggling to find the right words when you're trying to express your thoughts or ideas?

Um, no, not really. I mean, since I answer the phones and greet people all day, I kind of have to be pretty good at talking, right? I don't really struggle to find the right words at all. 

I can always explain what I'm trying to say, and I really try to make sure I'm being clear with everyone at the office. I definitely wouldn't want my boss or anyone to think I didn't know what I was talking about! So, yeah, no problems there. I hope I'm communicating clearly with you today, too? I'm really trying to give you good answers!
Do you think if you were more careful or paid closer attention, you would forget fewer things?

Um, well... I guess if I really, really focused more, maybe? But honestly, I don't think I forget all that much to begin with. 

I mean, I always try to be super careful at work. I keep my little sticky notes and my calendar updated so I don't miss anything important for the office. I definitely don't want anyone thinking I'm careless or dropping the ball, you know? I try so hard to stay on top of everything they give me. I might misplace a pen or something small every now and then, but nothing major! I think I do a pretty good job of keeping it all together. Is that... is that the kind of thing you meant? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea about how I work.
Do you think your forgetfulness is because you're not paying attention to the things you need to remember?

Um, no, I wouldn't say that at all. Like I said, I really don't think I'm very forgetful in the first place! 

I mean, I'm always trying my absolute best to pay attention to everything I need to do. When you work at a front desk, you have to be tuned in, right? So I'm always listening and trying to keep track of what people tell me. I really care about doing a good job and being reliable for my boss and everyone else. I definitely wouldn't want you to think I'm just zoning out and ignoring things I'm supposed to remember! I try really, really hard to be attentive. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining myself well enough for you.
Do you feel like you could remember things better if you tried harder?

Um, I mean, I really feel like I'm already trying as hard as I can. I put so much effort into making sure I remember everything I'm supposed to, especially at work. 

I don't think it's a matter of not trying hard enough, because I really do give it my all. I'd hate for anyone to think I'm not putting in the effort, you know? I want to be a good employee and a reliable person. I just... I don't think trying harder would change much because I'm already doing my best to keep everything straight. I hope you can see how much I care about getting things right? I'm really trying to be helpful here.
Do you think you would forget fewer things if you were to write down everything you need to remember?

Um, well, like I mentioned before, I actually do write a lot of things down already! I have my sticky notes and my calendar, and I'm always making sure they're updated. 

So, I don't really know if writing *everything* down would make a huge difference, just because I feel like I'm already doing a pretty good job of keeping track of the important stuff. I mean, I really try to be organized so I don't let anyone down at the office. I'd never want to be the kind of person who just lets things slip through the cracks. I think my system works pretty well for me, mostly? I hope that's a good way to handle it... do you think that's the right approach? I just want to make sure I'm doing what I'm supposed to be doing.
Do you think your forgetfulness is because you're not making enough of an effort to remember things?

Oh, gosh, no. Um... I really, really hope I'm not giving you the impression that I don't care or that I'm just slacking off. Because I honestly put a ton of energy into my job and making sure I'm on top of things. 

I'd be so embarrassed if my boss or—or even you—thought I wasn't trying my absolute hardest. Like we were just talking about, I feel like I'm constantly making an effort to be diligent and use my notes and everything. I just really want to be seen as a hard worker, you know? I really do give it my best shot every single day. I hope you can tell how much doing a good job matters to me? I really don't want you to think I'm just being lazy.
Does your forgetfulness happen in specific situations, like at work or in class, or can it happen at any time?

Um, I think... well, it's not like it's just one specific place. I guess it can happen anytime, really. But I mostly notice it at work because, you know, being an administrative assistant, keeping track of details is basically my whole job. 

But it's not like I'm constantly forgetting things everywhere I go! I mean, I manage my life pretty well, I think. It's just... sometimes a little detail might slip my mind, whether I'm at the office or just running errands. I really try not to let it affect my work, though. I want to make sure I'm always doing a good job for everyone. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Do you think that if you were in a quieter environment with fewer distractions, you would forget fewer things?

Um, I'm not really sure about that, to be honest. I mean... I wouldn't want to blame my office environment or anything. Everyone I work with is so great, and I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining about them being too loud or distracting. 

I think I handle the normal office noise pretty well? So, I don't really know if being in a super quiet room would actually make a difference for me. I've never really noticed the background noise being the reason I might lose track of a detail. I hope that's an okay answer? I just really wouldn't want to make excuses, you know? I feel like I should be able to do my job no matter where my desk is.
Do you think your forgetfulness is because you're preoccupied with other things when you're supposed to remember them?

Um, no, I don't think so? I mean, I really try to stay focused on whatever I'm doing, especially at work. I know how important it is to be present and pay attention to what people are telling me. 

I don't want you to think I'm just daydreaming or zoning out when I'm supposed to be listening. I really do try my best to give people my full attention. Sometimes things just sort of... slip away, I guess? But it's definitely not because I'm thinking about other things or not caring about what's going on. I hope you believe me on that? I really pride myself on being a good listener.
Do you think your forgetfulness is because you're not paying enough attention to details?

Um, I really hope it doesn't seem like I'm just being careless. I always, always try to pay attention to all the little details. That's so important in my job, and I'd hate for anyone to think I'm just brushing things off or not taking my work seriously. 

I mean, I really do try my hardest to catch everything. Sometimes a detail might just... get past me, I guess? But I promise it's not for a lack of trying or because I'm not paying attention on purpose. I really want to do a good job and make sure everything is right. Does that make sense? I just don't want to sound like I'm sloppy or anything like that.
Do you think your forgetfulness is more because you're not paying attention or because you're just not able to remember?

Um, oh gosh, that's a really hard question. I'm honestly not sure? I... I really, really hope it's not that I'm just not paying attention, because like I was saying, I do try so hard to stay focused. Being an admin assistant, it's my whole job to keep things running smoothly for everyone else, so I'd hate to think I'm just tuning things out. 

But I also don't know if I'd say I'm just unable to remember, either? Because I can remember a lot of things really well! It just feels like sometimes certain things just... don't stick, I guess? Even when I'm trying my absolute best. I don't really know how to tell the difference between the two, to be completely honest. I'm sorry, is it okay if I don't have a clear answer for that? I just really don't want to give you the wrong impression about my work ethic.
